This tutorial covers the design of large software systems: services that must stay fast, correct and available while
their load, their data and their failures grow. It has fifteen chapters, in reading order:

1. [Estimation and the design process](estimation-and-the-design-process/index.qmd): the design process, architectural
   characteristics and trade-offs, units and latency numbers, and estimates of load, availability and cost.
2. [The web stack](the-web-stack/index.qmd): the request path, load balancing, content delivery networks, stateless
   services, interfaces, real-time delivery, and authentication and authorisation.
3. [Performance and queueing](performance-and-queueing/index.qmd): latency, throughput and percentiles, Little's law,
   the M/M/1 queue, multi-server queues and capacity planning, and open and closed systems.
4. [Storage and databases](storage-and-databases/index.qmd): data models, schema design and normalisation, indexes and
   storage engines, transactions and isolation, file, block and object storage, and full-text search.
5. [Replication and partitioning](replication-and-partitioning/index.qmd): leader-follower, multi-leader and leaderless
   replication, ordering events, partitioning, secondary indexes, failure detection and unique identifiers.
6. [Consistency and consensus](consistency-and-consensus/index.qmd): consistency models, the CAP theorem, consensus,
   Paxos, Raft, coordination services and Byzantine faults.
7. [Caching](caching/index.qmd): where caches sit, eviction and hit ratio, invalidation and stampedes, distributed
   caches, and HTTP caching.
8. [Messaging and event streams](messaging-and-event-streams/index.qmd): queues, publish-subscribe, delivery semantics
   and idempotence, the partitioned log, failure handling, and event sourcing and change data capture.
9. [Distributed transactions](distributed-transactions/index.qmd): two-phase commit, global time and Spanner, sagas,
   the transactional outbox, and concurrency across services.
10. [Batch and stream processing](batch-and-stream-processing/index.qmd): MapReduce, pipelines and orchestration,
    analytical storage, stream processing, the Lambda and Kappa architectures, and approximate aggregation.
11. [Architecture styles](architecture-styles/index.qmd): components and coupling, layered and modular monoliths, the
    microkernel, microservices, event-driven and serverless architectures, and evolving an architecture.
12. [Reliability and operations](reliability-and-operations/index.qmd): SLOs and error budgets, fault tolerance,
    overload control, observability, safe change, multi-region deployment and security operations.
13. [ML, LLM and agent systems](ml-llm-and-agent-systems/index.qmd): the ML system, model serving, serving large
    language models, retrieval-augmented generation, agents, and operating AI systems.
14. [Case studies: infrastructure](case-studies-infrastructure/index.qmd): a URL shortener, a rate-limiting service, a
    key-value store, a notification service, a web crawler, a CDN, and counting and top-K.
15. [Case studies: applications](case-studies-applications/index.qmd): a news feed, chat, search autocomplete, media
    upload and streaming, file sync, collaborative editing with a convergent list CRDT, booking, and location services.

Each chapter sets out definitions and results, works through examples, and gives exercises to try. Results with a
published proof, such as Little's law, quorum intersection or the CAP theorem, are stated as theorems and proved, and
design patterns are stated as definitions. Quantitative examples and solutions are computed by code that runs, and
architectures are drawn as diagrams from their sources. The probability comes from
[Fundamentals of Mathematics for Physicists](../fundamentals-of-mathematics-for-physicists/index.qmd), and some
random processes and network models from [Complexity Science](../complexity-science/index.qmd).

::: {.start-reading}
The chapters are listed in reading order in the sidebar, followed by the [glossary](glossary/index.qmd). [Start with the notation →](notation/index.qmd)
:::

## Prerequisites

The chapters assume programming experience and the following chapters of the other tutorials, and link to them where a
result is used:

- [Probability](../fundamentals-of-mathematics-for-physicists/probability/index.qmd): independence, random variables,
  the exponential and Poisson distributions and limit theorems, for availability, queueing, hashing and sketches.
- [Random processes](../complexity-science/random-processes/index.qmd), [Networks](../complexity-science/networks/index.qmd)
  and [Dynamics on networks](../complexity-science/dynamics-on-networks/index.qmd) in Complexity Science: birth-death
  processes for queues, graphs and modularity for service dependencies, and random walks for crawling.

## Software

Every computation runs in plain Python 3.12, with [SimPy](https://simpy.readthedocs.io) 4.1.2 for discrete-event
simulation and the standard library's `sqlite3` for storage and indexing. Simulations use fixed seeds, so the recorded
outputs on the pages can be reproduced. Code that would need a live service, such as a database server, a message
broker or a load generator, is shown as illustrative code: it is marked as not run, and it has no recorded output.

Main libraries:

- [SimPy](https://simpy.readthedocs.io) 4.1.2: discrete-event simulation, for queues, retries, replication and
  consensus protocols.
- [`sqlite3`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/sqlite3.html): the SQLite database in the standard library, for
  schemas, indexes, transactions and full-text search.

Other libraries:

- [NumPy](https://numpy.org): arrays, random numbers and percentiles.
- [matplotlib](https://matplotlib.org): plots of the simulations.
- [D2](https://d2lang.com) v0.9.0: the language in which the architecture, data-flow and sequence diagrams are
  written.

The Python libraries are installed, at the versions the pages were computed with, into the `.venv-systems`
environment by one command run from the root of the [repository](https://github.com/georgedouzas/tutorials) (Python
3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) required):

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv-systems && uv pip install --python .venv-systems/bin/python -r system-design/requirements.lock
```

The diagrams are regenerated with D2 v0.9.0 on the `PATH`.

This tutorial has its own [glossary](glossary/index.qmd).
